meta.title: Nonja — a quiet inbox for macOS notifications
meta.description: No banners. Notifications collect quietly in the background, and you read them when you decide to. A menu bar app for macOS.

hero.title: Notifications can wait until you look
hero.tagline: Banners interrupt. Notification Center pours everything into one stream with no sense of read or unread and no way to deal with a batch. Nonja gives you somewhere else to look, and only when you ask.
hero.note: Free and open source. Apple Silicon

items.title: Collects quietly
items.body: Turn banners off in System Settings. Notifications still arrive in Notification Center, Nonja reads them from there and builds a list. Nothing appears on screen.

items.title: Groups by app
items.body: Not one timeline but a bundle per sender, and each bundle's heading clears that app's notifications in a single click.

items.title: Takes you to the source
items.body: Clicking a row presses the real notification, so you land wherever that app meant to take you — not just at its front door.

items.title: Shows no numbers
items.body: No badge count in the menu bar. A filled mark means something is waiting, an outline means nothing is. When something arrives, the shuriken turns once.

steps.title: Download the DMG
steps.body: Take the latest DMG from GitHub Releases and drag Nonja into your Applications folder.

steps.title: Allow it once
steps.body: The first launch is blocked, because Nonja is self-signed. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to the bottom, and click Open Anyway. Only the once.

steps.title: Grant the permissions
steps.body: Allow Full Disk Access and Accessibility. Then turn banners off in System Settings, which is what makes the whole thing worth having.

footer.built: Nonja is a tool built by one person. Notification + Ninja.
